The platform serves urban consumers across 720+ cities …

currentContext.business: Swiggy Limited operates a technology-led hyperlocal commerce platform that lets customers browse, select, order and pay for food, groceries and household essentials, with deliveries fulfilled through its on-demand delivery partner network. Established in 2013, it has diversified beyond food delivery into Swiggy Instamart (quick commerce for groceries and household essentials) and Swiggy Dineout (restaurant discovery, table reservations and dining experiences), and also provides advertising and visibility solutions to restaurant partners. The platform serves urban consumers across 720+ cities in India and partners with hundreds of thousands of restaurants, retail merchants, brand partners and delivery executives.

Food Delivery: Swiggy food delivery app and website
Advertising and visibility solutions for restaurant partners
Quick Commerce: Megapods (larger-format dark stores of approximately 8-10k sq. ft. housing up to 50k SKUs)
Supply Chain and Distribution: Swiggy Networks (Scootsy) warehousing, fulfilment and retail distribution services

currentContext.expansion: Swiggy is an asset-light platform whose expansion is expressed as network footprint rather than plant capacity. The overall platform now operates across 720+ cities in India, while Instamart, launched in 2020, has expanded to 125+ cities supported by 1,143 active dark stores. During FY 2025-26 the Company added 122 stores, taking active dark-store area to approximately 4.8 million sq. ft., growth of 21.1% YoY, and has introduced larger-format dark stores called megapods of approximately 8-10k sq. ft. capable of housing up to 50k SKUs, as assortment widened beyond grocery into non-grocery categories. Dedicated delivery infrastructure has brought Instamart delivery timelines down to approximately 13 minutes. Looking forward, the Business Outlook states that Swiggy remains committed to its long-term growth aspirations driven by continuous innovation, enhanced operational efficiency and well-planned expansion into new cities and regions; that it will continue investing in technology capabilities, AI-led solutions, automation and logistics infrastructure to improve scalability, operational productivity and customer experience; and that it is focussed on scaling Instamart through expansion of dark-store infrastructure. Group structure also expanded during the year, with Swiggy Instamart Private Limited becoming a step-down wholly owned subsidiary with effect from September 12, 2025, alongside existing subsidiaries Swiggy Networks Limited (formerly Scootsy Logistics), Supr Infotech Solutions Limited, Lynks Logistics Limited and Swiggy Neocap Private Limited, and associate Loyal Hospitality Private Limited. No plant, commissioning or capex-project timetable is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.note: The BRSR reports that 100% of the entity's turnover comes from a single business activity - other information service activities (food delivery and restaurant exploration) - so there is no product or activity diversification to buffer a shock to that one category.

Swiggy is a technology-driven, platform-based company operating solely in India across 35 locations (28 states and 7 Union Territories), with exports not applicable and no international offices or operations; performance is therefore fully exposed to Indian demand, regulation and competitive intensity.

Turnover for permanent employees was 34.87% in FY 2025-26 (34.72% male, 35.42% female), up from 33.37% in FY 2024-25, and 119.31% for other-than-permanent employees, which pressures institutional knowledge, hiring cost and execution continuity in a technology-led business.

risks.risk: Dependence on a value-chain delivery-partner network outside the formal workforce
risks.note: Delivery is fulfilled by an average of 6.49 lakh monthly transacting delivery partners who are classified as value chain partners and are explicitly not part of Swiggy's workforce; the Company engages no permanent workers, so service delivery depends on a contingent network it does not employ.

The BRSR turnover disclosure notes that the figures include revenue from operations that were discontinued effective 1 April 2026, and the quick-commerce business was housed in a newly created step-down subsidiary, Swiggy Instamart Private Limited, with effect from September 12, 2025 - a material reorganisation of where group revenue and losses sit.

Management flags that the global environment continues to face uncertainty from geopolitical tensions in West Asia, evolving trade restrictions and volatility in global commodity and energy markets, which have affected supply chains, moderated investment sentiment and created uneven growth conditions.

risks.risk: Concentration of workforce and reporting boundary in a few offices
risks.note: Of 68 offices as of 31 March 2026, four key offices each employing over 100 employees collectively account for more than 68% of Swiggy's workforce and core infrastructure, and these same offices define the environmental reporting boundary - a concentration of both operational capability and disclosure coverage.

risks.risk: Limited gender diversity at senior levels
risks.note: Women make up 18.72% of total employees, 12.5% of the Board of Directors and 25% of Key Management Personnel, and 100% of differently abled permanent employees are male, leaving the Company exposed on inclusion metrics it has itself made a stated priority.

one-line thesis: The contribution-margin repair job in Instamart is declared finished — the quarter closed at **-0.2% CM** after ~**INR30 of contribution per order** added over five quarters — and management is now deliberately spending that hard-won headroom back on growth, guiding to a **0 to -100bps CM band** and promising **more dark stores this quarter than in the previous four combined**. The bet is that the reset bought durable quality (M1 retention at a record **61% vs 55%** LY) rather than just a cleaner P&L, and that growth re-accelerates from a better base — four-week NOV growth has already snapped from **1% to 10%**. The credibility test is now sequenced and dated: cash breakeven ex-innovation in **two quarters**, food delivery margin **3% → 5%**, and a further **INR30/order** to QC EBITDA breakeven.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):

| Dark-store network utilisation | **~40%** | — | Individual stores hitting **2,500–3,000 orders/day** are maxing out, forcing new adds |

> Adjustments / one-offs called out on the call: (a) the **annual salary revision falls in the Q1 FY27 cycle** and sits *below* the contribution-margin line; (b) **minimum-wage hikes in certain states** raised picking/packing cost at warehouses and dark stores — management called it "not material" but confirmed it is baked into both Q1 actuals and Q2 guidance; (c) a **seasonal last-mile cost spike**, accentuated by the West Bengal election cycle, hotter-than-normal summer and harvest-season labour migration — the YoY dip narrowed to **20bps from 40bps** last year; (d) **Platform Innovation losses rose** on residual operating costs from the **Snacc closure** (shut last quarter) plus Toing user-acquisition marketing; (e) reported **platform frequency fell on mix**, not behaviour — the culled MTU base plus QC's structurally lower frequency; Toing volumes are excluded from reported B2C GOV.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Quick Commerce contribution margin:** explicit band of **0 to -100 bps** of NOV, from -0.2% exit. Stated on the assumption of **no change in competitive intensity** — "should things change dramatically, you should expect us to also keep moderating the strategy."
- **Quick Commerce NOV growth:** "cautiously optimistic of being able to deliver **at least double-digit growth on a sequential basis**, and hopefully more" for Q2 FY27. Supporting datapoint: trailing four-week NOV growth of **10%**, against **1%** in the preceding four weeks.
- **Food Delivery growth:** **18–20% YoY** maintained.
- **Food Delivery margin:** **~3% today → 5%**, described as a continuing steady climb.
- **Path to QC EBITDA breakeven:** a further **INR30 per order** of contribution, of which **~INR20 from monetization** — roughly **INR10 from brand/product margins and mix** and **INR10 from advertising**. Beyond breakeven, a **further INR25–30/order** to reach the steady-state EBITDA guidance. Management invited accountability: "you should hold us accountable to be able to deliver on these metrics."
- **Consolidated cash:** **breakeven at the overall cash level within the next two quarters**, excluding platform-innovation burn, funded by food-delivery margin accretion plus treasury income.
- **Store expansion:** **more dark stores added this quarter than in the last four quarters**, all inside **existing cities — no new cities**.
- **Capital Markets / Investor Day the following week**, where the full Toing explanation was deferred to.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxies management offered were (i) the **trailing four-week NOV growth of 10% vs 1%** in the prior four weeks — the freshest datapoint on the call and the basis for the double-digit sequential guide; (ii) **record M1 retention of 61%**, which management framed as the leading indicator of the transacting-user base compounding; and (iii) the **dark-store pipeline** — stores at 2,500–3,000 orders/day against ~40% network utilisation, i.e. capacity constraints are now localised rather than systemic.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Quick Commerce (Instamart).** The reset is complete: low-value users culled, CM at -0.2%, ~INR30/order of contribution added over five quarters. Take rate stepped up on three levers management called durable — **better negotiated brand margins as scale grows**, **advertising meaningfully kicking in**, and **improved user-fee monetization** after two quarters of no-fee experiments. New CEO **Nandita** appointed, chosen as a merchandising leader; her mandate was given as exactly two things: run the business/customer-and-brand experience ("zeroth priority") and scale the differentiated-assortment flywheel.
- **Food Delivery.** ~18% YoY adjusted growth, ~3% margin heading to 5%. Management's structural argument: **only ~1 in 10 Indians has ever transacted on a food-delivery platform**, and most of those at low frequency — so the category opportunity is secular and multi-year, and new competition will arrive in the **affordability** segment, not the premium one, "the premium segment is much harder to enter for any new competitor."
- **Toing (Platform Innovation).** A deliberately separate marketplace app, not "the same food delivery model transplanted to a new chassis." **Two of every three Toing users are new to Swiggy**; of the overlapping third, management sees two behaviours — users who simply prefer Toing as an alternative, and users splitting use-cases across the two apps. Launched with **minimal fixed-cost/overhead addition** — the cost is almost entirely user-acquisition marketing. Commissions **will be lower than Swiggy's but explicitly not zero**. Excluded from reported B2C GOV.
- **Snacc — exited.** The **micro-kitchen model was abandoned 4–5 months ago**; residual operating costs still hit this quarter. Management's post-mortem is unusually blunt and is a live read on competitors still pursuing it: it "requires a different kind of expertise", is "probably more expensive to build", and "the economics of that remain highly uncertain for most players."
- **Private label (Noice) & strategic brand partnerships.** The "Switch to Better" campaign is live on the Instamart storefront. The portfolio deliberately mixes **proprietary brands, large incumbents and challenger D2C brands** — atta partnered with **Aashirvaad/ITC**, eggs switching onto own-brand **Noice**. Many SKUs are outright exclusive; where they are not, the brand retails at an exclusive price. Management stated the private-brand strategy is **experience-driven, not value-driven**, and should carry **higher margins as it scales**.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Differentiated assortment as an alpha layer.** Management was careful to frame it as *additional*, not core: the base proposition ("20,000 assortment in minutes, in quality, on time") has its own organic growth rate; differentiation is "incremental growth on top" and, critically, differentiation not just against other quick-commerce apps but **against overall retail** — i.e. products a shopper cannot get anywhere else.
- **Advertising.** Named as ~INR10/order of the INR30 gap to EBITDA breakeven. The stated unlock is **product building** — adding inventory and app surfaces for brands to buy — not just harder negotiation.
- **Toing as a purpose-built affordability vehicle.** Management explicitly accepted the strategic premise behind the competitive threat ("affordability is a real need and should be improved to drive category growth") and is answering it with a separate app rather than degrading Swiggy's economics.
- **Density, not geography.** All store expansion stays inside existing cities — the growth option is depth of coverage and speed, not map expansion.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Balance-sheet position within the category.** Management's comparative claim was specific and repeated: "apart from Blinkit, many of the other competition is operating at **double-digit negative contribution margin**", against Swiggy's -0.2%. That gap — not scale — is what management says buys the flexibility to spend 0 to -100bps back on growth.
- **User quality as an asset built the hard way.** M1 retention at 61% vs 55% LY came *after* deliberately culling low-value users and accepting soft growth for two quarters. Management's read on any rival attempting the same reset is that they "are going to see significant dips in volumes" — a moat by virtue of having already paid the cost.
- **Accounting conservatism as a differentiator.** Under direct questioning, the CFO stated Swiggy capitalises **none** of employee salary costs, token/compute costs, or new-store pre-opening costs — "even if there are 30-60-90-day period, all of that gets baked into our contribution margin" — and denied any securitisation of payables. Both were framed against practices attributed to unlisted competitors, i.e. the reported CM is claimed to be a cleaner number than peers'.
- **Zero-commission scepticism grounded in structure.** "If it is zero commission, then who pays for cost of the platform. Somebody has to pay." Management noted platforms marketing zero commission still charge for delivery, which at low AOVs "do not really reflect a zero commission structure."
margins & cost dynamics:
The take-rate improvement is the quarter's central margin fact: QC revenue grew ~13% QoQ against ~3% NOV growth. Management attributed it to three stacked, **annual-cycle** levers — brand margin renegotiation (which happens on annual, not quarterly, cycles, "depending on the cycle of those respective brands"), advertising scale-up, and user-fee monetization after the no-fee experiments were reversed — and asserted flatly that these are durable: "these are revenues that we have been able to establish with the brand partners as well as on the consumer side. So we don't expect these to turn."

On the cost side, the planned CM give-back of 0 to -100bps is earmarked to three named line items, all customer-experience rather than discount-led: (i) **fixed cost of newly opened dark stores**, (ii) **network speed and monsoon-season serviceability** ("better-than-competition, including serviceability"), and (iii) **selection availability**, after a "completely hard reset". Notably absent from the list: consumer discounting. Wage inflation (annual revision plus state minimum-wage hikes) and the seasonal last-mile spike were both absorbed, with the last-mile YoY dip halved to 20bps through efficiency.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Dark stores:** Q2 FY27 will add **more stores than the last four quarters** did — the single most checkable capex claim on the call. Trigger is demand, not land-grab: individual stores hitting **2,500–3,000 orders/day** in hyperlocal catchments.
- **No new cities.** Expansion is densification inside the existing footprint. Network-level utilisation ~**40%**, so the aggregate network is not capacity-constrained — the adds are surgical.
- No absolute capex figure, store count or cost-per-store was given on the call.
capital allocation: The stated funding architecture: food delivery's margin accretion (3% → 5%) plus treasury income cover the quick-commerce EBITDA journey, delivering **consolidated cash breakeven ex-innovation within two quarters**. Platform Innovation is explicitly ring-fenced and *not* pre-committed capital — "once the product hits both Product Market Fit as well as what we call Business Market Fit, that is when it will get its growth capital, and it will have its own economics from there on." Snacc is the precedent that this gate has teeth: it was shut rather than funded. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary.
risks & watch-items:
- **The CM band is conditional.** The 0 to -100bps guide assumes **no change in competitive intensity** and management pre-committed to moderating if it changes — so the guide is a plan, not a floor. Watch whether Q2 lands inside the band or gets re-based.
- **Seven-to-eight-player market.** Management explicitly refused the comfort that a single competitor's funding squeeze changes the category: "I don't think it is only one player that changes how we execute… There are seven players." A tight funding environment for unlisted rivals may *not* rationalise discounting.
- **Growth is being bought.** Contribution is being deliberately spent down from a barely-positive base. If the four-week 10% NOV signal does not persist, the company will have given up margin without buying growth.
- **App-rating deterioration.** An analyst flagged a fall in both the level and quality of Swiggy app ratings. Management's answer was that they see nothing unusual but "we're going to look into this… we'll report our findings." An open, unresolved item — check whether they report back.
- **Positioning coherence.** The same analyst noted the strategy has cycled through Maxxsaver → removing delivery charges → own brands. Management conceded Maxxsaver "should have been seen more as a tactic than a strategy" and that "we could have done even more to cement more distinctive positioning for Instamart." That is a real admission of prior strategic drift.
- **Instamart leadership transition.** A new CEO plus "some other changes in leadership at Instamart… a few people across different roles" — execution risk precisely as the growth pedal goes down.
- **Private label vs advertising conflict.** Own brands cannibalise ad-sellable inventory and compete with the very brands buying ads. Management's answer (private-label margins are structurally higher, so the trade is favourable) is an assertion, not yet evidenced.
- **Toing's unit economics are unproven.** Pressed on how lower commissions and lower fees still cover a ~INR50–60 delivery-partner cost, the answer was that AOVs differ and "we don't need to make INR40 per order in this business" — directional, not demonstrated.
management quality / tone: Notably non-defensive and specific for a company under competitive pressure. Three tells. Second, when Vijit Jain pushed on whether 61% retention was "gold standard," Majety declined the flattering framing outright — "I don't think this is gold standard… safe to say we are not done here" — and elsewhere conceded past positioning failures in the first person. The bet is that the reset bought durable quality (M1 retention at a record **61% vs 55%** LY) rather than just a cleaner P&L, and that growth re-accelerates from a better base — four-week NOV growth has already snapped from **1% to 10%**. The credibility test is now sequenced and dated: cash breakeven ex-innovation in **two quarters**, food delivery margin **3% → 5%**, and a further **INR30/order** to QC EBITDA breakeven.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Quick Commerce contribution margin:** explicit band of **0 to -100 bps** of NOV, from -0.2% exit. Stated on the assumption of **no change in competitive intensity** — "should things change dramatically, you should expect us to also keep moderating the strategy."
- **Quick Commerce NOV growth:** "cautiously optimistic of being able to deliver **at least double-digit growth on a sequential basis**, and hopefully more" for Q2 FY27. Supporting datapoint: trailing four-week NOV growth of **10%**, against **1%** in the preceding four weeks.
- **Food Delivery growth:** **18–20% YoY** maintained.
- **Food Delivery margin:** **~3% today → 5%**, described as a continuing steady climb.
- **Path to QC EBITDA breakeven:** a further **INR30 per order** of contribution, of which **~INR20 from monetization** — roughly **INR10 from brand/product margins and mix** and **INR10 from advertising**. Beyond breakeven, a **further INR25–30/order** to reach the steady-state EBITDA guidance. Management invited accountability: "you should hold us accountable to be able to deliver on these metrics."
- **Consolidated cash:** **breakeven at the overall cash level within the next two quarters**, excluding platform-innovation burn, funded by food-delivery margin accretion plus treasury income.
- **Store expansion:** **more dark stores added this quarter than in the last four quarters**, all inside **existing cities — no new cities**.
- **Capital Markets / Investor Day the following week**, where the full Toing explanation was deferred to.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxies management offered were (i) the **trailing four-week NOV growth of 10% vs 1%** in the prior four weeks — the freshest datapoint on the call and the basis for the double-digit sequential guide; (ii) **record M1 retention of 61%**, which management framed as the leading indicator of the transacting-user base compounding; and (iii) the **dark-store pipeline** — stores at 2,500–3,000 orders/day against ~40% network utilisation, i.e. capacity constraints are now localised rather than systemic.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Quick Commerce (Instamart).** The reset is complete: low-value users culled, CM at -0.2%, ~INR30/order of contribution added over five quarters. Take rate stepped up on three levers management called durable — **better negotiated brand margins as scale grows**, **advertising meaningfully kicking in**, and **improved user-fee monetization** after two quarters of no-fee experiments. New CEO **Nandita** appointed, chosen as a merchandising leader; her mandate was given as exactly two things: run the business/customer-and-brand experience ("zeroth priority") and scale the differentiated-assortment flywheel.
- **Food Delivery.** ~18% YoY adjusted growth, ~3% margin heading to 5%. Management's structural argument: **only ~1 in 10 Indians has ever transacted on a food-delivery platform**, and most of those at low frequency — so the category opportunity is secular and multi-year, and new competition will arrive in the **affordability** segment, not the premium one, "the premium segment is much harder to enter for any new competitor."
- **Toing (Platform Innovation).** A deliberately separate marketplace app, not "the same food delivery model transplanted to a new chassis." **Two of every three Toing users are new to Swiggy**; of the overlapping third, management sees two behaviours — users who simply prefer Toing as an alternative, and users splitting use-cases across the two apps. Launched with **minimal fixed-cost/overhead addition** — the cost is almost entirely user-acquisition marketing. Commissions **will be lower than Swiggy's but explicitly not zero**. Excluded from reported B2C GOV.
- **Snacc — exited.** The **micro-kitchen model was abandoned 4–5 months ago**; residual operating costs still hit this quarter. Management's post-mortem is unusually blunt and is a live read on competitors still pursuing it: it "requires a different kind of expertise", is "probably more expensive to build", and "the economics of that remain highly uncertain for most players."
- **Private label (Noice) & strategic brand partnerships.** The "Switch to Better" campaign is live on the Instamart storefront. The portfolio deliberately mixes **proprietary brands, large incumbents and challenger D2C brands** — atta partnered with **Aashirvaad/ITC**, eggs switching onto own-brand **Noice**. Many SKUs are outright exclusive; where they are not, the brand retails at an exclusive price. Management stated the private-brand strategy is **experience-driven, not value-driven**, and should carry **higher margins as it scales**.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Differentiated assortment as an alpha layer.** Management was careful to frame it as *additional*, not core: the base proposition ("20,000 assortment in minutes, in quality, on time") has its own organic growth rate; differentiation is "incremental growth on top" and, critically, differentiation not just against other quick-commerce apps but **against overall retail** — i.e. products a shopper cannot get anywhere else.
- **Advertising.** Named as ~INR10/order of the INR30 gap to EBITDA breakeven. The stated unlock is **product building** — adding inventory and app surfaces for brands to buy — not just harder negotiation.
- **Toing as a purpose-built affordability vehicle.** Management explicitly accepted the strategic premise behind the competitive threat ("affordability is a real need and should be improved to drive category growth") and is answering it with a separate app rather than degrading Swiggy's economics.
- **Density, not geography.** All store expansion stays inside existing cities — the growth option is depth of coverage and speed, not map expansion.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Balance-sheet position within the category.** Management's comparative claim was specific and repeated: "apart from Blinkit, many of the other competition is operating at **double-digit negative contribution margin**", against Swiggy's -0.2%. That gap — not scale — is what management says buys the flexibility to spend 0 to -100bps back on growth.
- **User quality as an asset built the hard way.** M1 retention at 61% vs 55% LY came *after* deliberately culling low-value users and accepting soft growth for two quarters. Management's read on any rival attempting the same reset is that they "are going to see significant dips in volumes" — a moat by virtue of having already paid the cost.
- **Accounting conservatism as a differentiator.** Under direct questioning, the CFO stated Swiggy capitalises **none** of employee salary costs, token/compute costs, or new-store pre-opening costs — "even if there are 30-60-90-day period, all of that gets baked into our contribution margin" — and denied any securitisation of payables. Both were framed against practices attributed to unlisted competitors, i.e. the reported CM is claimed to be a cleaner number than peers'.
- **Zero-commission scepticism grounded in structure.** "If it is zero commission, then who pays for cost of the platform. Somebody has to pay." Management noted platforms marketing zero commission still charge for delivery, which at low AOVs "do not really reflect a zero commission structure."
margins & cost dynamics:
The take-rate improvement is the quarter's central margin fact: QC revenue grew ~13% QoQ against ~3% NOV growth. Management attributed it to three stacked, **annual-cycle** levers — brand margin renegotiation (which happens on annual, not quarterly, cycles, "depending on the cycle of those respective brands"), advertising scale-up, and user-fee monetization after the no-fee experiments were reversed — and asserted flatly that these are durable: "these are revenues that we have been able to establish with the brand partners as well as on the consumer side. So we don't expect these to turn."

On the cost side, the planned CM give-back of 0 to -100bps is earmarked to three named line items, all customer-experience rather than discount-led: (i) **fixed cost of newly opened dark stores**, (ii) **network speed and monsoon-season serviceability** ("better-than-competition, including serviceability"), and (iii) **selection availability**, after a "completely hard reset". Notably absent from the list: consumer discounting. Wage inflation (annual revision plus state minimum-wage hikes) and the seasonal last-mile spike were both absorbed, with the last-mile YoY dip halved to 20bps through efficiency.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Dark stores:** Q2 FY27 will add **more stores than the last four quarters** did — the single most checkable capex claim on the call. Trigger is demand, not land-grab: individual stores hitting **2,500–3,000 orders/day** in hyperlocal catchments.
- **No new cities.** Expansion is densification inside the existing footprint. Network-level utilisation ~**40%**, so the aggregate network is not capacity-constrained — the adds are surgical.
- No absolute capex figure, store count or cost-per-store was given on the call.
capital allocation: The stated funding architecture: food delivery's margin accretion (3% → 5%) plus treasury income cover the quick-commerce EBITDA journey, delivering **consolidated cash breakeven ex-innovation within two quarters**. Platform Innovation is explicitly ring-fenced and *not* pre-committed capital — "once the product hits both Product Market Fit as well as what we call Business Market Fit, that is when it will get its growth capital, and it will have its own economics from there on." Snacc is the precedent that this gate has teeth: it was shut rather than funded. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary.
risks & watch-items:
- **The CM band is conditional.** The 0 to -100bps guide assumes **no change in competitive intensity** and management pre-committed to moderating if it changes — so the guide is a plan, not a floor. Watch whether Q2 lands inside the band or gets re-based.
- **Seven-to-eight-player market.** Management explicitly refused the comfort that a single competitor's funding squeeze changes the category: "I don't think it is only one player that changes how we execute… There are seven players." A tight funding environment for unlisted rivals may *not* rationalise discounting.
- **Growth is being bought.** Contribution is being deliberately spent down from a barely-positive base. If the four-week 10% NOV signal does not persist, the company will have given up margin without buying growth.
- **App-rating deterioration.** An analyst flagged a fall in both the level and quality of Swiggy app ratings. Management's answer was that they see nothing unusual but "we're going to look into this… we'll report our findings." An open, unresolved item — check whether they report back.
- **Positioning coherence.** The same analyst noted the strategy has cycled through Maxxsaver → removing delivery charges → own brands. Management conceded Maxxsaver "should have been seen more as a tactic than a strategy" and that "we could have done even more to cement more distinctive positioning for Instamart." That is a real admission of prior strategic drift.
- **Instamart leadership transition.** A new CEO plus "some other changes in leadership at Instamart… a few people across different roles" — execution risk precisely as the growth pedal goes down.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
